title: The shipped plugin assigns no model or effort to its AI-judgment roles on either host
symptom: The Claude readability-inspector sets effort: medium and no model, so it inherits the caller. The Codex inspector pins gpt-5.6-terra/medium only in a development definition; the Codex plugin manifest declares skills and no agents, so the shipped Codex plugin assigns nothing. The few AI-judgment steps (row design, one-file inspection, boundary reconciliation) therefore run on whatever the session happens to use, and token cost per step is unmeasured.

rootCause.summary: No single source stores model and effort per role and host, and the Codex plugin format cannot carry agent definitions. Confirming requires measured per-role usage and an engine-ground-truth evaluation; see the proposal.

requestedOutcome: Each AI-judgment role that the plugin owns has a documented model and effort per host, generated from one source, chosen by evaluation against the engine's deterministic result, with the author role left to the user's session.
decisions: 2026-10-22 user direction: put model and effort assignment per host into a design proposal and open this issue; optimize the model that each host's AI uses.
The plugin never overrides the author role's model (proposal principle 1); this is a design position pending user confirmation.

actions.description: Write the design proposal with host capability facts, a single-source generation scheme and an evaluation plan.
Study the open-source Gajae Code (Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code, clone e9179a1) for how it stores per-role model and effort for Codex and Claude.

Move column-set candidates (guide --authoring columnSets and axisNotes for TypeScript) and requested-boundary reconciliation (check --expect-axis axisExpectation) from agent judgment into engine output.
Record per-step token usage from session records, usage numbers only.
Evaluate Claude and Codex inspector candidates against engine ground truth, then add product/models.json with generation and a contract test.
Add product/models.json, validation, in-place stamping through sync:plugin and a contract test; ship the Claude inspector model and effort from it.

history.summary: User asked how model distribution should be optimized per host and to record model and effort for each AI-judgment role on Claude and Codex.

Measured host facts: Claude accepts model and effort frontmatter in the validator; the Codex manifest has skills only, so Codex values need documentation or an installer-written global agent file. Open-source Gajae Code stores per-role provider/model[:effort] selectors in its own ~/.gjc/agent config and never writes Codex model_reasoning_effort; it only merges managed entries into ~/.codex/hooks.json. No effort is written into Codex's own config by that project.

Added product/models.json with capability-checked assignments, development/tools/model-assignments.ts, in-place stamping in sync:plugin and test/model-assignments.test.ts. The Claude inspector now ships model: sonnet with effort: medium as unevaluated defaults. The author role is refused by validation. Codex values reach only the development definition because the plugin manifest ships no agents. Fallback ladder, engine-side judgment, usage recording and evaluation remain open.

Added columnSets and axisNotes to guide --authoring for TypeScript (empty for other languages) and check --expect-axis with an axisExpectation block (covered, missing, unknown) that never changes the exit status. SKILL.md steps 1 and 5 and docs/user/modes.md describe both. Usage recording and the evaluation remain open.
